TITLE: UK MPs are turning on PM Starmer — now analysts say he's unlikely to last the year
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-12T07:37Z (updated 13:55Z)
AUTHOR: Holly Ellyatt (CNBC)

KEY POINTS:
- U.K. Prime Minister Keir Starmer's leadership is hanging by a thread.
- Analysts have slashed the odds of Starmer facing a leadership challenge by September.

EURASIA GROUP (analysts led by Mujtaba Rahman, emailed analysis): raised the probability of Starmer being ousted this year to 80%, up from 65% previously. Conversely, only a 20% chance of Starmer remaining PM.

EURASIA SCENARIO PROBABILITIES:
- 35%: MPs will force a leadership election by September
- 25%: orderly transition in which Starmer agrees to stand down
- 20%: immediate leadership election

JORDAN ROCHESTER (head of EMEA fixed income, currency and commodity strategy at Mizuho): "For many, the writing is on the wall at this stage, it's just a matter of how quickly the exit happens... [Nonetheless] If Starmer goes, it will make history. No sitting Labour PM yet has ever faced a leadership challenge or been removed by his party."

DEUTSCHE BANK STRATEGISTS: rise in the interest rate on the U.K.'s 10 and 30-year borrowing costs, to 5% and 5.67%, respectively on Monday, reflected market concerns that a new Labour leader "may face pressure to ease the fiscal rules and raise gilt issuance."

EURASIA: "Starmer's attempt to quell a rebellion against his leadership has failed... Although he may remain a few more months in Downing Street, he is still fighting for his political life after his make-or-break speech earlier Monday did not include enough new policies to satisfy many Labour MPs."
